chunks: He remained in Baghdad for twelve years after the death of his teacher al-Sayyid, independently assuming the leadership, then departed from it after that.

key_terms.السَّيِّدِ: al-Sayyid — title referring to Sayyid al-Murtada 'Alam al-Huda (d. 436 AH), the eminent Shia theologian and jurist who was Shaykh al-Tusi's primary teacher
key_terms.بِالزَّعَامَةِ: al-za'amah — the overall religious, scholarly, and communal leadership (marja'iyya) of the Shia community
key_terms.مُسْتَقِلًّا: independently — as sole supreme authority, without deferring to any other senior scholar

ai.seo_question: How long did Shaykh al-Tusi remain in Baghdad after the death of his teacher al-Sayyid al-Murtada, and why did he eventually leave?
ai.summary: This biographical note records that Shaykh al-Ta'ifa Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Tusi remained in Baghdad for twelve years following the death of his foremost teacher al-Sayyid al-Murtada 'Alam al-Huda (d. 436 AH/1044 CE), during which he independently led the Shia scholarly community as its supreme authority. He subsequently departed Baghdad — driven out around 448 AH by Seljuk-era sectarian unrest — and settled in Najaf al-Ashraf, where he founded what became the enduring centre of Shia learning.
